title: Add invocation cohorting and kernel-warmup heatmap with adaptive alert backoff
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add new per-invocation cohorting metadata, a Grafana kernel-warmup heatmap dashboard, and an adaptive alert backoff policy to reduce noisy alert churn for long-tail cohorts.
description: Motivation: We see repeated noisy alerts driven by small cohorts of invocations (odd prompt shapes or very long KV cache cold starts). Teams need a way to attribute cost/latency anomalies to invocation cohorts and to visualize how kernel latency evolves across the first N tokens as kernels and KV caches warm up. This PR introduces: 1) a lightweight per-invocation cohorting tag (invocation_cohort_id) based on prompt-shape and context-warmth heuristics; 2) a kernel-warmup heatmap that aggregates kernel-level latency for the first 32 tokens vs KV-warmth buckets and exposes a Grafana dashboard; 3) an adaptive alert-backoff rule that quiets alerts for cohorts that show high variance but low long-term impact, and increases sampling and digesting instead of immediate paging. Checklist: - [x] Add cohort id generation and propagation into traces and metrics - [x] Emit cohort-level rollup counters and histograms (latency, tokens, cost-est) - [x] Instrument kernel-level per-token timings and KV-warmth tag - [x] Grafana dashboard JSON and panels for heatmap + cohort explorer - [x] Alert rule: adaptive backoff with cohort decay window and prioritization - [x] Unit tests and integration test for cohort assignment - [x] Docs: observability guide section + example query snippets Design summary: - Cohorting: we compute a compact prompt-shape fingerprint = hash(num_tokens, avg_token_length, normalized_prompt_embedding_bucket) and combine with a KV-warmth score (0..3) to form invocation_cohort_id = fingerprint:vwarm. This is intentionally coarse to bound cardinality while grouping meaningful shapes. Cohort id is attached as a trace tag and a metric label for rollups. - Kernel warmup heatmap: the collector records per-kernel micro-latency for token positions 0..31 and emits a histogram keyed by (kernel_name, token_pos_bucket, kv_warmth). We downsample high-frequency kernels with reservoir sampling for storage cost. - Adaptive alert backoff: new alert logic uses cohort-level variance + recent impact to decide whether an alert should escalate to paging or be converted into a digest entry. This reduces churn for cohorts with spiky behavior but small aggregate cost. Commits (high-level): - commit 1: "observability: add invocation cohort id and cohort propagation" - introduces cohort fingerprinting code, tagging in request tracer, and metric label plumbing. - commit 2: "collector: kernel warmup timing and kv-warmth tag" - records per-token kernel latencies, adds reservations for high-cardinality limits, and backfills unit tests. - commit 3: "monitoring: grafana kernel-warmup heatmap + cohort explorer" - adds dashboard JSON + example queries. - commit 4: "alerting: adaptive cohort backoff rule and playbook" - updates alert rules and runbook guidance. Files changed (high level): - src/observability/cohorting.rs: new fingerprinting and tag propagation logic - src/collector/kernel_timer.cc: per-token kernel timers and kv-warmth extraction - src/collector/rollups.rs: cohort rollup counters and histograms - deploy/monitoring/grafana/dashboards/kernel_warmup_heatmap.json: new dashboard (heatmap + cohort explorer panels) - infra/alerts/alert_rules.yaml: adaptive backoff rule and new labels - sdk/python/redwood/observability.py: helper to surface cohort id in SDK traces - docs/observability/cohorting.md: design/queries and runbook - tests/observability/test_cohorting.py: unit tests for fingerprint boundaries - examples/observability/query_examples.md: example PromQL / Flux queries Migration notes: - Cohort id is an additive label; existing metrics are unchanged but rollups gain a new label. We add default cardinality caps to collectors (default 5k cohorts per shard) to avoid explosion; teams with high cardinality can opt-in for higher caps via config. Observability queries (examples included in docs): - Top cohorts by token-cost: sum(token_cost) by (invocation_cohort_id) - Kernel warmup heatmap: heatmap of p95 kernel_latency per token_pos_bucket grouped by kv_warmth - Cohort stability metric: delta of p95 over 5h-window and 1h-window Review summary: - Diego found an edge-case where trivial prompt shapes collided; we widened the hash input to include a small fingerprint of the first non-empty token. - Priya suggested lowering reservoir sample size for the hottest kernels; adjusted to 10k -> 5k to cap storage. - Liam requested an explicit opt-out flag for compliance-sensitive customers; added config flag and test. Backwards compatibility: additive only. Telemetry and cost: added a small instrumentation overhead (~0.7% sampling equivalent) when heatmap enabled; default is off for low-traffic tiers. Merge: Squashed and merged to main on 2026-02-24.
review_comments: Diego Alvarez: Nice approach on bounding cardinality. One concern: two very different prompts with identical token counts and avg_token_length might collide. Can we include a tiny prefix fingerprint?
Maya Chen (author): Good catch — added first-nonempty-token fingerprint (8-bit) into the prompt-shape hash to reduce that class of collisions. Updated tests accordingly.
Priya Natarajan: Reservoir sampling tune looks fine but storage hit still non-trivial for high-throughput kernels. Suggest exposing sample_limit per-kernel via config and a safe default of 5k.
Maya Chen (author): Exposed kernel_sample_limit in collector config; default 5k. Added integration test to simulate high-frequency kernel and assert retention bound.
Liam O'Connor: For enterprise/private installs we need an opt-out to avoid sending cohort fingerprints to hosted telemetry. Add config and docs.

Maya Chen (author): Added 'observability.cohorting.enabled' config toggle and doc section for compliance. The toggle disables cohort label emission while keeping internal behavior for on-prem aggregation.
